chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from ʿUthmān, from Ibn Muskān, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
If a man kisses a woman with desire, or touches her private part, he repeats the wudu (ablution).

The proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it as indicating a form of recommendation, or as meaning that he washes his hand, and that is called wudu, as has been stated earlier. That which indicates this interpretation is...

key_terms.التَّأْوِيلِ: interpretation or reconciliatory reading of the report
key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: the report or hadith under discussion
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), here discussed as being repeated or understood in a broader sense
key_terms.شَهْوَةٍ: sexual desire or lustful intent in the act mentioned

ai.seo_question: Does kissing with desire or touching the private part require repeating wudu in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling related to kissing with desire and touching a woman's private part in relation to wudu (ablution). The compiler then explains that the apparent command to repeat wudu should be understood either as recommendation or as referring to washing the hand, which may also be termed wudu in this context.
